premise: The rocket's tanks are nearly empty; Excavator digs up a chunk of ice in the crater's shadow, and the ice turns out to be rocket fuel.
inspiration: Aesop's 'The Crow and the Pitcher' (the clever way to what you need), turned: the answer is in the ground, in the dark.
lesson: The answer is sometimes right beneath your feet.
learning: Water ice from the Moon can be split into gases that make rocket fuel.

en-US.title: Ice for the Rocket
en-US.text: The {rocket:enter} {rocket:go to pad} rocket stood on the pad with its fuel tanks nearly empty. {rocket:shake} How would it ever fly home? {engineer:enter} {engineer:face happy} Engineer tapped her helmet. The answer is in the crater, she said. {excavator:enter} {excavator:go to crater} Excavator trundled down into the shadows and {excavator:live} dug. Scrape… scrape… scrape… {canvas:glints 10s} Something glittered. {ice:enter} Ice! Water ice, hidden in the dark where the Sun never shines. {ice:live hold} It sparkled as the light caught it. {engineer:face surprised} Water can be split into two gases, said Engineer, and those two gases make rocket fuel. {engineer:face happy} So they melted it, and split it, and filled the tanks, drop by drop. {excavator:pulse} [excited] Three, two, one… {sfx:rumble} {rocket:live} The rocket fired its engines, just to test. {all:face happy} Enough to get home, said Engineer. [laughs] And a little extra, to come back.

es-ES.title: Hielo para el cohete
es-ES.text: El {rocket:enter} {rocket:go to pad} cohete esperaba en la plataforma con los depósitos casi vacíos. {rocket:shake} ¿Cómo iba a volver a casa? {engineer:enter} {engineer:face happy} Ingeniera se dio un golpecito en el casco. La respuesta está en el cráter, dijo. {excavator:enter} {excavator:go to crater} Excavadora bajó traqueteando hasta las sombras y {excavator:live} cavó. Rasca… rasca… rasca… {canvas:glints 10s} Algo brilló. ¡{ice:enter} Hielo! Hielo de agua, escondido en la oscuridad donde nunca da el sol. {ice:live hold} Destellaba cuando le llegaba la luz. {engineer:face surprised} El agua se puede separar en dos gases, dijo Ingeniera, y con esos dos gases se hace combustible para cohetes. {engineer:face happy} Así que lo derritieron, lo separaron y llenaron los depósitos, gota a gota. {excavator:pulse} [excited] Tres, dos, uno… {sfx:rumble} {rocket:live} El cohete encendió los motores, solo para probar. {all:face happy} Suficiente para volver a casa, dijo Ingeniera. [laughs] Y un poquito más, para regresar.

rumble.prompt: a deep, soft rocket engine rumble felt through the ground, steady and warm, not loud or scary
